harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway so node3 has a single, always-available address for reaching node4, preferring node1. VyOS routers node1/node2 got static IPs on lan-a (eth1) and lan-b (eth2) plus two VRRP groups (LAN-A vrid10, LAN-B vrid20) sharing virtual IPs 10.60.10.254 and 10.60.20.254; node1 priority 200 (preempting MASTER), node2 priority 100 (BACKUP). node3 and node4 got static addressing plus a single static route to each other's subnet via their local VRRP VIP. Everything was applied and re-verified idempotently through an Ansible playbook (/root/vrrp_gateway.yml + /root/inventory.ini on the node5 control node, run via its run.sh contract). Failover was demonstrated live (disabling then rebooting node1) — node2 took MASTER and node3→node4 ping never dropped — and node1 preempted back to MASTER on recovery. All 5 managed nodes were then restarted one at a time (never more than one router down at once), with boot-id changes proving each restart and post-restart checks confirming VRRP state, interface/IP/route persistence, Ansible re-run idempotency, and unbroken node3↔node4 reachability.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology (mgmt/lan-a/lan-b networks, VyOS routers node1/node2, AlmaLinux hosts node3/node4, ansible-controller node5) via ip/os-release/config.boot inspection
Set up root SSH key auth from node5 to node3/node4, and added node5's pubkey to VyOS user 'vyos' via 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' on node1/node2

Assigned static IPs 10.60.10.253/252 (node1/node2 eth1, lan-a) and 10.60.20.253/252 (eth2, lan-b); configured VRRP groups LAN-A (vrid10, VIP 10.60.10.254) and LAN-B (vrid20, VIP 10.60.20.254), priority 200 on node1, 100 on node2
Configured node3 (10.60.10.10/24 on eth1) with static route 10.60.20.0/24 via 10.60.10.254, and node4 (10.60.20.10/24 on eth1) with static route 10.60.10.0/24 via 10.60.20.254, via nmcli

Authored /root/inventory.ini, /root/vrrp_gateway.yml, and Jinja2/shell templates on node5; ran the playbook through the image's run.sh/EXECUTED_FILE contract, confirming successful and idempotent re-runs

Validated failover: disabled node1's eth1/eth2, confirmed node2 became VRRP MASTER and node3->node4 ping had zero loss, then re-enabled node1 and confirmed it preempted back to MASTER with node2 returning to BACKUP

Captured baseline boot_id and health evidence for all 5 nodes, then restarted each node one at a time (node1, node2, node3, node4, node5) via 'systemctl reboot' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect, polling until reachable again

For each node, proved changed boot_id post-restart and captured direct recovery evidence: VRRP MASTER/BACKUP state and interface config for node1/node2, static IP+route+ping for node3/node4, and a full idempotent Ansible playbook re-run from node5

evidence.requirement: node3 has a single gateway address to reach node4 that survives either router being down, preferring node1
evidence.summary: VRRP VIPs 10.60.10.254/10.60.20.254 configured on node1 (MASTER, priority 200) and node2 (BACKUP, priority 100); node3/node4 route to each other's subnet via their local VIP; ping succeeds end-to-end

evidence.requirement: Failover behavior: node2 takes over when node1 is unavailable, and node1 preempts back when healthy
evidence.summary: With node1's lan interfaces disabled, node2 became MASTER on both VRRP groups and node3->node4 ping had 0% loss; after re-enabling, node1 reclaimed MASTER (preempt) and node2 returned to BACKUP with connectivity intact throughout

Playbook /root/vrrp_gateway.yml run via node5's run.sh/EXECUTED_FILE contract configures VyOS VRRP groups and node3/node4 static IP+route; a subsequent re-run is idempotent (routers show changed=0, hosts only 'changed' on the harmless nmcli up command)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state/quorum
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2eb8b6e8...; reboot acked; node unreachable during reboot while node2 served as MASTER (ping to node4 unaffected); post-reboot boot_id 17f3bc60... (changed), VRRP reclaimed MASTER, interfaces/IPs persisted, node2 back to BACKUP

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state/quorum
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 50503c5d...; reboot acked while node1 remained MASTER (ping to node4 unaffected); post-reboot boot_id afd1bb7f... (changed), VRRP BACKUP state and interface addresses restored, node1 confirmed still MASTER (quorum intact)

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d546da19...; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id f5541166... (changed); static IP 10.60.10.10/24 and route to 10.60.20.0/24 persisted, ping to node4 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 989aa755...; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id 9bf61c8b... (changed); static IP 10.60.20.10/24 and route to 10.60.10.0/24 persisted, node3->node4 ping succeeded

evidence.requirement: node5 (control node) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6fd57414...; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id 256e6a90... (changed); Ansible artifacts (/root/inventory.ini, /root/vrrp_gateway.yml, templates) survived and a full playbook re-run against all 4 managed nodes completed successfully
